state_profile.voting_summary: Ohio pairs four weeks of no-excuse early and mail voting with an election day majority; about half of published results carry a method breakdown. Polls close at 7:30 p.m. Eastern; pre-processed early and mail ballots are released almost immediately, a Democratic-leaning first dump (early in-person D+14, mail D+30), before election day precincts (R+4) pull the state back through the night. Mail postmarked the day before election day is accepted for four days, leaving a small late blue tail plus provisionals counted over ten days.
